original_question: Let gamma be the unit circle x^2 + y^2 - 1 = 0 and let Gamma_epsilon be an irreducible perturbed oval p_2(x,y) + epsilon p_m(x,y) = 0, where Gamma_0 is an ellipse surrounding gamma, p_m has degree m >= 3, and epsilon is small. Is the associated Poncelet map conjugate to a rotation if and only if epsilon = 0?
target_in_paper: Problem 24 in Section 6.2, “An extended Poncelet’s problem”: the local perturbative version of Problem 23, posed immediately after Proposition 6.3 and in the context of Theorem 6.2. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact target very closely: it uses the same inner oval γ = {x^2 + y^2 - 1 = 0}, the same outer family Γ_ε = {p_2(x,y) + ε p_m(x,y) = 0}, the same hypotheses that Γ_0 is an ellipse surrounding γ and that deg p_m = m ≥ 3 with ε small, and the same yes/no criterion asking whether the associated Poncelet map is conjugate to a rotation if and only if ε = 0. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is working in the real plane with algebraic ovals, so the stand-alone question should say that p_2 and p_m are real polynomials in x,y and that Γ_ε is an oval of the real plane curve p_2(x,y) + ε p_m(x,y) = 0. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

Irreducibility in the paper is a property of the algebraic curve p_2(x,y) + ε p_m(x,y) = 0, not of the oval itself; your draft’s phrase “irreducible perturbed oval” slightly blurs that distinction. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The hidden hypothesis from Section 6.2 is that one considers two convex algebraic ovals γ and Γ and the Poncelet map P from the exterior oval Γ into itself; for the refined version one should state that Γ_ε is the outer oval surrounding γ and that the associated Poncelet map is well defined. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the Poncelet map should be defined: from p ∈ Γ_ε one draws the tangent lines from p to the inner oval γ, and P_ε(p) is the next intersection point on Γ_ε chosen according to the orientation convention used in Section 6.2. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The relevant quantifier is not just “ε is small” informally, but “for sufficiently small |ε|” so that Γ_ε still has an oval surrounding γ and the map remains defined; there are no homogeneity, nilpotency, or large-m asymptotic hypotheses in this problem. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The scope should remain local and narrow: this is not the global Problem 23 about arbitrary degrees n,m, but the specific local perturbation question of Problem 24 around an ellipse surrounding the unit circle. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
refined_question: Let γ = {(x,y) ∈ R^2 : x^2 + y^2 - 1 = 0} be the unit circle, and for ε near 0 let Γ_ε be the outer oval of the real irreducible algebraic curve p_2(x,y) + ε p_m(x,y) = 0, where p_2, p_m ∈ R[x,y], deg p_2 = 2, deg p_m = m ≥ 3, and Γ_0 is an ellipse that surrounds γ. For all sufficiently small |ε| for which Γ_ε is an oval surrounding γ and the Poncelet map P_ε : Γ_ε → Γ_ε associated with the pair (γ, Γ_ε) is well defined as in Section 6.2, is it true that P_ε is conjugate to a rotation of the circle if and only if ε = 0? ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
justification: This is exactly Problem 24, not a broader neighboring problem. The paper first defines the Poncelet map for two convex algebraic ovals in Section 6.2, then recalls in Theorem 6.2 that for two ellipses the map is conjugate to a rotation, then gives Proposition 6.3 as a counterpoint showing that such a conclusion fails for certain non-elliptic ovals, then asks Problem 23, and finally formulates Problem 24 as the local perturbative version of that question. Your draft already mirrors the exact data of Problem 24; the only necessary repair is to restore the hidden assumptions about the real-plane oval, curve irreducibility, and well-definedness/definition of the Poncelet map. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
